insights.so_what: Revenue is concentrated enough that losing a few hundred accounts would be material; retention spend on this group has the highest return.
insights.why: A wholesale-heavy customer mix: median 12 orders and GBP 4,629 spend versus 2 orders and GBP 674 overall.
insights.now_what: Stand up named-account coverage for the 558 Champions before the next Q4 peak, and add a churn alert when a Champion's recency exceeds 60 days.

insights.finding: 34% of customers never place a second order; the 1st->2nd step loses 1,493.
insights.so_what: At GBP 481 AOV that is GBP 717,933 of un-realised second-order revenue in a single year.
insights.why: Median gap to a second order is 50 days -- long enough that there is a real reactivation window, and no evidence of a geographic cause (UK 65.6% vs RoW 65.8%).
insights.now_what: Trigger a reorder prompt at day 40, before the median gap closes. A 5pp lift is worth roughly GBP 104,000/year.

insights.finding: The 70% December revenue 'collapse' is a partial-month artefact, not a business event.
insights.so_what: Any decision taken on the raw month-on-month chart would be a reaction to a reporting bug.
insights.why: The extract ends 9 days into December; pro-rated, December runs +2.2% against November.
insights.now_what: Label or exclude partial periods in every recurring report. One-line change to the reporting layer.

insights.finding: Model recall on male passengers is 0.417 versus 0.867 on female passengers.
insights.so_what: The aggregate metric hides a subgroup where the model is barely better than the base rate. Any decision applied uniformly would fail one group.
insights.why: Male survival is 20% in the holdout; the model has little signal to separate the rare positives within that group.
insights.now_what: Either report per-group metrics alongside the headline, or set a group-specific threshold. Do not ship a single global threshold silently.

insights.finding: The survival model's holdout PR-AUC is 0.791 versus 0.867 in cross-validation.
insights.so_what: The CV number overstates real-world performance by ~0.08 PR-AUC. Promoting on the CV figure would set expectations the model cannot meet.
insights.why: 179 holdout rows is a small sample, and hyperparameters were selected on the same CV folds that produced the 0.867.
insights.now_what: Report the holdout figure externally. Treat the CV figure as a model-selection tool only.

insights.finding: Hybrid retrieval scores 0.739 MRR versus 0.562 for dense-only, but the cross-encoder rerank *reduced* it to 0.711.
insights.so_what: Adding a reranker on best-practice grounds alone would have made this system measurably worse.
insights.why: ms-marco-MiniLM is trained on web-search passages; this corpus is terse technical prose with heavy vocabulary overlap.
insights.now_what: Keep hybrid retrieval, drop the reranker, and re-test if the corpus character changes.

checks.note: Both tracks trace to a stated business question in Phase 1.
Both datasets hashed (SHA-256) and version-pinned; the mart's exclusions are reconciled to the raw feed with zero residual.
Every cleaning statistic is fit on train only; target encoding is cross-fitted. Leakage inflation measured at +0.081 corr.
The tuned-vs-untuned CV gain (+0.016) is smaller than fold noise (+/-0.022). Reported as 'no measurable gain', not as an improvement.
Holdout PR-AUC 0.791 is materially below CV 0.867 on n=179. Stated explicitly rather than smoothed over.
Male-passenger recall 0.417 is close to unusable. Blocks promotion to any automated decision.
Every chart is annotated with its finding; the colourblind-safe Okabe-Ito palette is used throughout.
9 cleaning decisions plus a separate assumptions log.
Seeded, pinned, hashed; one command reruns the whole pipeline.

translation.technical: The HistGradientBoostingClassifier pipeline achieved a cross-validated PR-AUC of 0.867 (sigma 0.022) under stratified 5-fold CV, though the held-out estimate regressed to 0.791, indicating the hyperparameter optimisation overfit the validation folds. Slice-level diagnostics reveal heteroscedastic performance: recall on the male stratum is 0.417 versus 0.867 on the female stratum, and the Brier score of 0.158 implies the posterior probabilities are poorly calibrated for downstream thresholding.
translation.business: Our model correctly ranks who survived about 79% of the time on data it has never seen. In testing it looked better than that, so we are reporting the lower, more honest number. It works well for women, and much less well for men, where it catches under half of the cases it should. We would not yet use its confidence scores to make an automatic decision; we would use its ranking to prioritise a human review.
